To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

mianserin is an antidepressant drug which, like amitripty-line, increases frequencies below 6 hz, decreases those from 7 to 15 hz, and increases frequencies above 18 hz, with a peak EEG effect at 2 to 4 hours, a pattern of measured change that parallels plasma levels and a time course for EEG effects similar to that of amitriptyl-line.
mianserin is a new putative thymoletic drug with a high cerebral penetrance, and that its pharmacokinetics, EEG, and behavioral effects show a time course similar to that of plasma concentrations.

mianserin, a new antidepressant agent with a novel chemical structure, was found to have a pharmacokinetic profile in man that included rapid and extensive absorption, peak levels at two hours, an apparent volume of distribution in the range 3,000 to 5,000 l, and a half-life of 9 to 12 hours.

the study of the pharmacokinetics and EEG effects of the antidepressive drug, mianserine, and with the relationship between EEG and behavioral effects.
the development and application of new methods for the analysis of EEG data.
the effects of the thymoleptic drug, mianserine, on the human electroencephalogram (EEG) and on vigilance measures.

the pharmacological profile of the compound mianserin (Org 3770) is similar to that of amitriptylinoxide and differs from that of imipramine and chlorpromazine.
mianserin has a profile of EEG effects which is similar to that of the tricyclic antidepressants, and the drug has high cerebral penetrance and a long plasma half-life.
